summary:
I tested HEAD 26b3952 as a self-contained single-file exe, which I published myself into a folder whose path has a space. It was launched through ProcessStartInfo.Arguments, Start-Process and cmd /c on this PC's NTFS, with real deny rules, and against the C:\ root as a Medium-integrity ordinary account. I compared it with base aa3d96b, built from git archive.

All 14 acceptance criteria are met:
- Finish lines 1-4: the trailing-backslash line exits 0 on all three routes, with the control's core (Completed, 20 files, 4 folders). The spaced root with an `out  dir` report folder writes at the exact two-space path. `"<tree>\"` alone keeps its window up past 3 s. `"<tree>\" extra --report` exits 2 at 142 ms with no window.
- Deny-CreateFiles folder: exit 3 at 157 ms with no window. The base build reached exit 3 only at 945 ms, after its window had opened at 620 ms.
- `"C:\" --report C:\r.json`: exit 3 at 145 ms, with no scan and no C:\r.json.
- Planted links: links planted mid-scan at the old fixed `<report>.tmp` and at `<report>` itself never wrote through, and the sentinel was unchanged. CreateNew refuses a file, a hardlink, a symlink to an existing file, a junction and a directory symlink. It follows a dangling symlink, which is the residual the design records. File.Move(overwrite) replaces a hardlink, a symlink or a dangling symlink at `<report>` as an entry.
- Tests and rules: the whole suite passes 1443 of 1443, the slice's Core tests pass 63 of 63, the four exe facts pass, Fitness reports all 114 rules holding, and the window cases C-007, C-008, C-012 and O-016 pass.

Two problems remain in what was written, and both already have fix obligations owed to build-slice that the tree does not yet answer:
- **(1) Regression IN-M1 / O-045 (defect).** `<tree>\" --report <r>`, with no opening quote, is split cleanly by Windows into 3 arguments, and the base build ran it in report mode (exit 0 at 1455 ms, root `tree\`). On HEAD the repair joins them into one argument, `--report` disappears, and the published exe hangs with its window up (window at 391 ms, still running at 6 s, no report). The unit-level experiment shows the same for `D:\Data\" --report "out.json` and `D:\Data\" --report "C:\out\" x`. The batch idiom `%~dp0"tree"` is improved: base hangs, HEAD exits 0.
- **(2) Create-only folder / O-046, O-051; this disproves O-042.** This is a folder with Deny FILE_DELETE_CHILD on the folder and an inherited Deny DELETE on its files. The probe passes, the window opens at 379 ms, the scan runs, the app exits 3 at 751 ms, and `.fsa-<hex>.tmp` is left behind. The base build did the same (it left r.json.tmp), so the late exit predates the slice. The slice's own precondition and Write's 'a temporary that was made is removed' contract are still false there.

Notes:
- My first exe-script run errored on DirectoryInfo.GetAccessControl, which .NET does not have; I switched to FileSystemAclExtensions. It errored before any ACL rule was applied, so nothing was left set.
- Every deny rule I set was removed, and all scratch data under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\fsa-validate-sl007 was deleted.
- The worktree is unchanged apart from .taad-scratch.
- No loop in the slice history: there is one build attempt, and it changed src.

criteria.criterion: 1. Split the command line when a quoted root ending in one backslash is followed by --report and a path ("D:\Data\" --report out.json, "C:\" --report C:\r.json)
criteria.how: Measured: CommandLine.Arguments on the CommandLineToArgvW argv gives [D:\Data\, --report, out.json] and [C:\, --report, C:\r.json]. On the published exe the C:\ line reached report mode and was refused at 145 ms. CommandLineTests passes.

criteria.criterion: 2. Split it when the root and a quoted report path both have spaces, with a run of two spaces in the report path
criteria.how: Measured: argv(2) is repaired to [D:\My Data\, --report, C:\out  dir\r.json] with both spaces kept. The published exe wrote at \out  dir\l2.json.

criteria.criterion: 3. Split it when a quoted root ending in a backslash has nothing after it, so argv's only '"' is its last character
criteria.how: Measured: argv <D:\Data"> is repaired to [D:\Data\]. CommandLineTests.AQuotedRootEndingInABackslashAloneIsTheFolder passes.

criteria.criterion: 4. Split it when Windows split the line cleanly and no '"' is left in argv
criteria.how: Measured: "D:\Data", "D:\Data\\", unquoted C:\ and the root-last line come back unchanged. CommandLineTests.ALineWindowsSplitCleanlyIsReturnedAsItCame (same instance, line not read) passes.

criteria.criterion: 5. Split it when the typed line does not account for argv, so alignment fails: an inner '"' gives null, a trailing-only '"' gives argv unchanged
criteria.how: Unit level only: CommandLineTests.ALineThatDoesNotMatchItsArgvIsRefusedOrLeftAlone passes (63 of 63). No dotnet-muxer launch was made.

criteria.criterion: 6. Split it on the grammar the new tokeniser opens: two \" in one line, an odd run of three, an even run, a tab, quoted and unquoted argv0, an empty quoted value, a non-ASCII root, UNC and \\?\, the root last, and corpus roots A01-A10 hand-quoted
criteria.how: TheGrammarTheRepairOpensIsSplitAsTyped and EveryRootOfTheCorpusHandQuotedIsRepairedByArguments pass. Measured myself: two \" in one line gives [D:\A\, --report, E:\out\]; the root last is kept; the odd run of three exits 0 on the exe with root tree\\\.

criteria.criterion: 7. Unattended report from cmd or Start-Process: the exe started as "<tree>\" --report "<file>" (finish line 1)
criteria.how: Published single-file exe in a spaced folder, via ProcessStartInfo, Start-Process and cmd /c: exit 0 in 713-832 ms, Completed, 20 files, 4 folders, the same core as the control.

criteria.criterion: 8. Unattended report with a spaced quoted root and a report folder with two spaces (finish line 2)
criteria.how: Published exe via psi and Start-Process: exit 0 at about 770 ms, the report at the exact 'out  dir' path, root 'tree sp\'.

criteria.criterion: 9. Open the window on a folder given at launch: the exe started as "<tree>\" alone (finish line 3)
criteria.how: Published exe: window at 379 ms, still running at 3033 ms. I did not read which root the window shows (no UI driven); the argv unit row gives <tree>\ and QuotedRootShapesTests passes.

criteria.criterion: 10. Refuse a report line it cannot take: "<tree>\" extra --report "<file>" (finish line 4)
criteria.how: Published exe: exit 2 at 142 ms, no window, no report.

criteria.criterion: 11. Refuse a report path it cannot write when the folder exists but denies CreateFiles, as an ordinary user meets with C:\ --report C:\r.json
criteria.how: Published exe: the Deny CreateFiles folder gives exit 3 at 157 ms with no window (base: 945 ms, after its window opened). The real "C:\" --report C:\r.json as a Medium-integrity account gives exit 3 at 145 ms. A create-only folder, which this criterion does not cover, is still refused late (see checks and O-042).

criteria.criterion: 12. Probe and temporary in a writable folder: each open draws its own name at that moment, the probe leaves nothing, and a failed move removes the temporary
criteria.how: ReportFileTests (fresh stem per open, counting fact, probe leaves the folder as it was, AFailedMoveLeavesNoTemporary) pass. No .fsa-* entry was left in any writable folder after the exe runs.

criteria.criterion: 13. Write without writing through a link already at the target name: a hardlink, symlink or junction at the temporary, a hardlink or symlink at <report>, or a hardlink at the old fixed <report>.tmp
criteria.how: Measured: CreateNew refused a hardlink, a symlink to an existing file, a junction and a directory symlink with the sentinel unchanged, and Move replaced the links at <report>. On the exe, a hardlink planted mid-scan at r.json.tmp and at r.json left the sentinel ORIGINAL, and r.json was its own single-link file. The ReportFileTests rows pass.

criteria.criterion: 14. Write without writing through a dangling symlink planted at the temporary's exact fresh name
criteria.how: The design fixed this case as a residual held by the name, not by CreateNew. I measured that CreateNew does follow a dangling symlink at a known name (it created the target). What holds the case is that the stem is drawn just before each open and shown to nobody: corpus rows T07/E01-E03 and AFreshStemIsDrawnForEachOpenAtTheMomentOfOpening pass. I could not plant at a name nobody can predict, so this is code-level.

obligations.evidence: Raw FileStream CreateNew in scratch: an existing file, a hardlink and a symlink to an existing file gave IOException; a junction and a directory symlink gave UnauthorizedAccessException. The sentinel stayed ORIGINAL and nothing was created in the junction target. ReportFileTests.AWriteRefusesALinkAlreadyAtItsTemporaryName passes. A dangling symlink is followed, as the design records (T07); it is not part of this precondition.

File.Move(tmp, report, overwrite:true) onto a hardlink, a symlink and a dangling symlink at report replaced each one as an entry: sentinel ORIGINAL, report a regular file holding the new JSON, no dangling target created. On the published exe, a hardlink and a dangling symlink planted at r.json mid-scan gave exit 0, sentinel ORIGINAL, and r.json a 3948 B single-link regular file.

Disproved on the published exe. In a create-only folder (Deny FILE_DELETE_CHILD on the folder, inherited Deny DELETE on its files) the probe passed, the window opened at 379 ms, the app scanned, exited 3 at 751 ms and left .fsa-d4758142592b4504ad15524a81acf3a2.tmp. So the probe does not need the DELETE right the write's move is checked for.

Still open in the tree. tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/CommandLineUnpairedQuoteTests.cs does not exist. CommandLine.Arguments on 'app.exe D:\Data\" --report out.json' returns the one argument <D:\Data\ --report out.json>. The published exe hangs on <tree>\" --report <r> (window at 391 ms, running at 6 s), while base aa3d96b exits 0 at 1455 ms.

Still open. tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/ReportFileDropFolderTests.cs does not exist. ReportFile.Probe (ReportFile.cs:57-68) still opens with FileShare.None and never deletes through a second open. The create-only folder run exits 3 late and leaves .fsa-*.tmp.
Same finding as O-046 and the same measurement: probe unchanged, late exit 3 at 751 ms after the window, temporary left in the folder.

not_reached: Which root the interactive window actually shows for "<tree>\" alone. I saw only that a window opened and stayed up; I drove no UI and ran no hook mode that reads the window.

A real shared or drop folder written to mid-scan by another account (the SC-037 threat with a real second principal watching the folder). Plants here were made by this same account, at the known old name and at <report>.
A real create-only drop folder as found on a file server or set by another administrator. The create-only shape was simulated with deny rules on a scratch folder.
Launch routes other than ProcessStartInfo, Start-Process and cmd /c: Task Scheduler, services, Explorer shortcuts, and the dotnet muxer (not launched).
Other Windows builds and ucrtbase versions. This PC runs Windows 11 10.0.26300 and ucrtbase 10.0.26100.9711 (N-065); not measurable on this machine.
WindowMutants NoCrashHandler and NoExitRule. Not run.
WindowCases C-007, C-008, C-012 and O-016 ran on artifacts/publish built at 09:16, before the comments-only commit 26b3952. My own HEAD publish was used for every other exe run.
An elevated run of the shipped exe. Out of scope here, and not on the named elevation list.
